title: Refitted Bootstrap and Selected-Clipping Limits for Quantile Treatment Effects on the Treated
banked_reason: Typed D0.5: faithful and mathematically sound selected-trim QTT package achieves subfield below required field floor; exact quadratic chart, public-grid-determined variance ranking, open nonidentical-tie scalar law, and absent reproducible coverage/length comparisons limit reach (score ceiling 6.5<7.4; no bounded in-scope upgrade).
gap_reasons: The exact propensity chart and known uniform covariate distribution remain substantive scope restrictions after the first-derivative extension.
Because limiting variances share a common law-dependent multiplier, the optimal coordinate is determined by the public grid, limiting the substantive adaptation supplied by data-driven selection.
The scalar law at nonidentical variance ties remains unresolved, while maximum-calibrated coverage avoids that question.
The projected score reflects this restricted reach and the absence of reproducible coverage and length comparisons establishing the practical value of the conservative maximum interval.
proof_attempt_summary: A D-1.2 restoration replaced a laundered Gaussian frontier with the launched selected-trim QTT program. D0 proved the joint marked-infinitely-divisible law, fully refitted unrestricted m-out-of-n bootstrap, positive-gap selector limit, and maximum-calibrated exact-tie interval; the sixth-moment kill test passed, and the cited standard lemmas were verified from primary sources. D0.5 found the result sound and faithful but graded its novelty subfield, below the required field floor, because the exact quadratic chart and public-grid-determined selector limit broader reach; the nonidentical-tie scalar law remains open.
tldr: The causal target is the quantile treatment effect on the treated population. The proved result gives the common marked-Poisson \(n^{1/3}\) law of the finite clipping-coordinate vector after the public slope projection, retaining random fitted-slope noise, and the exact coupled truncation error \(\mu_2J/(H^2\sqrt\lambda R)\). It establishes uniform conditional Wasserstein convergence and second-moment transfer for the fully refitted with-replacement bootstrap for every \(m\to\infty\), \(m/n\to0\). A positive public grid variance gap yields a consistent selected coordinate and its explicit non-Gaussian law. The full-vector maximum interval has uniform coverage at least \(90\%\), including exact ties, and length at most \(2R_{\mathrm{cap}}n^{-1/3}\) for every realized sample and calibration draw. A separately proved first-derivative common-margin corollary carries these four conclusions to the larger class allowing zero boundary drift. The selected scalar law at a tie between different projected kernels is the sole residual question.
gap: Practical selected-trim QTT reporting lacks a complete joint corrected-grid quantile inversion and refitted bootstrap second-moment theorem for this quadratic-tail benchmark.
fill: The project derives the common infinitely divisible vector and clipping drift from primitives, transfers the entire feasible procedure through with-replacement resampling for every \(m/n\to0\), and calibrates uncertainty through the full coordinate maximum.
